# CLAIMs with `works` `governance-of-becoming`

*Works — A manuscript the record's claims are marshalled into. Membership says a claim is in the work; whether the record believes it is the status, and the two disagree (ADR-032).*

**The Governance of Becoming** — the owner's article series, requested at U31 of the exchange "Memes, Contracts, and Systemic Normativity" and proposed by ChatGPT on 2026-11-24 (A49) as fourteen articles and reordered at U32 (A51, the order the owner took on 2026-11-25), with governance-of-possibility as its Article 2, to be collected as The Governance of Becoming: Individuation, Interdependence, and the Organization of Possibility; its precursor draft is the manuscript Becoming Through One Another (A26 to A28), requested at U20. Organizations individuate through maintained relationships that make their processes mutually consequential, store work, distribute authority and create dependencies, implicit contracts among them; cooperation changes its participants, so exploitation, domination and agency without answerability can arise from success; normative governance is the legitimate organization of those transformations, including the capacity to discover and correct them, and constitutional regeneration is its political form. Its argument is held mainly in the lines distributed-agency, dependence-and-domination, organizational-normativity and will-organization.

| [CLAIM-603](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) v8 | The supply, not the loss, decides dependency | The assistant's, on the owner's remark of 2026-11-05 that "assured help makes recipients lose skill" sounds "closely related to niche differentiation and specialization phenomena". The record holds the biology. On the Black Queen Hypothesis ([THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)) a cell that stops making a leaky public good saves its cost while others still supply it, so the loss is favoured to the individual and spreads. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. The Samaritan's dilemma has the same logic (Ostrom et al.), and Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's recipient is better off in the high-aid state. The loss itself is not the pathology. What differs is the supply. A Black Queen loss stops by itself when helpers grow rare, because the helpers are the same population. Aid is set from outside and does not fall as dependence grows, so nothing stops the loss short of what aid covers, and withdrawal returns the cost ([CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md)). Buchnera's loss runs both ways, and the result is interdependence. A state that taxes its citizens (Moore) is in the same position: it lost nothing, it exchanges. After the owner linked the claim to the gift economy of Burning Man, readings of Mauss, of St John on Burning Man and of Heins, Unrau and Avram added two things. One-way supply costs the receiver standing as well as capacity: in Mauss the unreturned gift makes its receiver inferior. And the return need not go back to the giver: it can travel round a circuit, as Mauss's do, or out to a whole community, as Burning Man's is meant to, and both sit beside a demand for self-reliance. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
